name: What should I consider when choosing bathroom flooring for accessibility?

mainEntity.name: What should I consider when choosing bathroom flooring for accessibility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard tile installation can present trip hazards and slick surfaces for individuals with mobility challenges. To improve accessibility, consider zero-threshold transitions flush with adjoining bedroom or hallway flooring to allow easy walker or wheelchair access. Opt for textured, slip-resistant porcelain tiles or smaller mosaic patterns where frequent grout lines provide natural traction when wet. Additionally, planning subfloor framing carefully ensures adequate support for future equipment or curbless shower walk-ins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Focus on high-traction, slip-resistant tile finishes and flush, zero-threshold transitions that eliminate tripping hazards for walkers and wheelchairs.
